mutants.reason: Line 226 is only reached in InitAckWait. In ot_gpio_nnc the receiver has ping_req_i=1'b0 and init_trig_i=MuBi4False. So ping_rise is always 0 and ping_pending_q is always 0 (ping_pending_d = ping_rise | (... & ping_req_i & ...)). Both '||' and '&&' give send_ping=0, so the ping line never differs.

The filter's stored value resets to 1 instead of 0. If CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER is enabled within about 15 cycles of reset while i_gpio is 0, DATA_IN reads 1 (and a spurious falling/rising event can follow) until the counter updates the stored value. This is a legal stimulus, and the difference appears on the ports.

op_full feeds only instr_wr_err inside tlul_err, and a_config_allowed does not use it. instr_wr_err only matters when instr_type is MuBi4True. In that case tlul_adapter_reg already raises instr_error, because en_ifetch_i is tied to MuBi4False. err_internal is the OR of these, so d_error and the register effects are identical. i_a_instr is a single bit, so instr_type is never invalid.

The read-data mux uses unique case (1'b0) instead of (1'b1). It selects the first register whose hit bit is 0, which is normally register 0. Reads then return the wrong data, for example INTR_STATE contents for every offset, and reset values, read-back and wo/reserved reads all break.

Unused leaves of the one-hot tree (OneHotWidth is 114, tree width 128) are tied to 1 instead of 0. The spurious write-enable check then always flags an error, which latches into intg_err_o and raises the fatal alert. o_alert pulses with no integrity fault or ALERT_TEST write.

Line 84 is in the 'default' branch (a_size=3). There mask_chk stays 0, so a_config_allowed = addr_sz_chk & mask_chk & ... is 0 whether addr_sz_chk is 0 or 1. err_o and d_error are therefore unchanged.

The software/hardware priority in prim_subreg_arb is inverted. A software write now loads the hardware d value, normally 0, and not the written data. Writes to the registers (DIRECT_OUT, DIRECT_OE, INTR_ENABLE and others) therefore do not take effect.
and_tree only feeds addr_err, and prim_reg_we_check instantiates prim_onehot_check with AddrCheck=0. addr_err is tied to 1'b0 and and_tree is unused, so err_o does not depend on this line.

The default ack_pd is 1, so the receiver holds ack high even with no alert. The four-phase handshake no longer completes: the sender cannot see the ack fall. Repeated alert pulses (fatal alert repeated until reset, repeated ALERT_TEST pulses) are lost, and the handshake behaviour is wrong.

One ECC bit of prim_secded_inv_64_57_enc (data_o[60]) is no longer inverted. The command integrity generator and the response integrity generator then disagree with the decoder-based checkers. Every request looks like a command integrity error (spurious alert), and o_d_intg_err goes to 1.
outstanding_q is cleared instead of set on an A handshake. d_valid never rises, so no request ever gets a response, and the host never sees d_source, d_size, d_opcode or d_error.

mubi4_test_false_loose now returns True==val. With en_ifetch_i tied to MuBi4False, instr_error becomes 0, so an instruction-fetch Get (i_a_instr=1) is answered with d_error=0 and data instead of d_error=1. This is a legal stimulus and differs at the ports. The spec does not require this error to be checked (GP-10-19), only that fetch errors are covered (GP-9-06).
